Joktheel
JOK-theh-el
proper noun
A city in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah; also the name King Amaziah gave to the rock-city Selah of Edom after he took it. The name is taken to mean “subdued by God” or “the blessedness of God.”

Biblical Definition

Joktheel is a city in the lowland of Judah, named in the roll of Judah’s inheritance: “And Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel” (Jos 15:38). The same name meets us again in a striking act of King Amaziah of Judah, who “slew of Edom in the valley of salt ten thousand, and took Selah by war, and called the name of it Joktheel unto this day” (2Ki 14:7). The name is taken to mean subdued by God, and Amaziah’s renaming of the Edomite stronghold declares the confession that it was God who subdued it — the victory was the LORD’s, not the arm of the king. Yet the history warns as loudly as it teaches. This same Amaziah, flushed with the conquest, carried home the gods of Edom and bowed himself before them, and his end was ruin and a conspirator’s sword. To name a fortress “subdued by God” and then worship the gods of the subdued is the height of folly and ingratitude. The lesson of Joktheel is that every victory the believer wins is God’s subduing, and must be answered not with pride nor with borrowed idols, but with worship of the LORD alone who gave it. The name preaches; the man’s later apostasy is the counter-sermon.

Webster 1828 Definition

A lowland city of Judah; also the name Amaziah gave to the Edomite rock Selah after conquering it, confessing that God subdued it.

JOKTHEEL, a city in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah.

The same name was given by King Amaziah to Selah of Edom, which he took by war (2Ki 14:7).

The name is taken to mean subdued by God, or the blessedness of God.

Amaziah’s renaming confessed the victory to be the LORD’s.

Yet Amaziah then worshipped the gods of conquered Edom, to his ruin.

Key Scripture

Jos 15:38 — "And Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel,"

2Ki 14:7 — "He slew of Edom in the valley of salt ten thousand, and took Selah by war, and called the name of it Joktheel unto this day."

2Ch 25:14 — "Now it came to pass, after that Amaziah was come from the slaughter of the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them."

Psa 44:3 — "For they got not the land in possession by their own sword, neither did their own arm save them: but thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, because thou hadst a favour unto them."

Modern Corruption

A city of Scripture whose name means “subdued by God”; it rebukes the pride that claims the victory as its own and the folly of Amaziah, who worshipped the gods of the people he conquered.

expand to see more

Joktheel faces no postmodern redefinition, but its history names a live corruption: the pride that ascribes to its own strength the victories that are God’s, and the strange folly of honoring the very idols of a defeated foe. Amaziah named the rock “subdued by God” and then bowed to the gods of Edom.

The principle to recover is that every conquest is God’s subduing, and calls for worship of the LORD alone. The believer wins no battle by his own arm; and to answer God’s deliverance with pride, or with the borrowed idols of the world he has overcome, is ingratitude that ends in ruin. Not by their own sword got they the land, but by the LORD’s right hand.

Hebrew Roots

A lowland town of Judah, and the name Amaziah gave to conquered Selah of Edom; it means “subdued by God.”

Usage

"Amaziah named the Edomite rock Joktheel, subdued by God."

"Every victory is the LORD’s subduing, not the strength of the arm."

"To worship the idols of a conquered foe is ingratitude unto ruin."
